# Scan page three paths Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan.

**Goal:** The published scan page explains the three paths after a person decides (known typology, new red flag,
new method), with each path's steps, live figures and a "what each path changes" table; the walkthrough gains a
dated banner linking to it.

**Architecture:** Everything is generated by the two existing builders (`tools/build_scan_demo.py`,
`tools/build_walkthrough.py`) from constants and imported data, and checked by their existing guards
(`evals/check_scan_demo.py`, `evals/check_walkthrough.py`). The existing publishers and staleness gates carry the
pages to the portfolio. No new page, no new publish path.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3 stdlib (fc-08 `.venv` at `~/fc-08-schedule/.venv`), inline SVG, vanilla JS in the page.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-31-scan-page-three-paths-design.md`

## Global constraints

- Work in the FULL clone `~/fc-08-scan-mechanics`, branch `sdd/scan-page-three-paths`. Never a linked worktree.
- Python: `~/fc-08-schedule/.venv/bin/python` (the system python lacks `claude_agent_sdk`).
- Commits: `PATH=~/fc-08-schedule/.venv/bin:$PATH env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY git commit`, explicit staging, never
  `-a`, never `--no-verify`, no Co-Authored-By trailer.
- No `.bak` / `_backup` / `_before_*` files.
- Nothing is published, and nothing reaches the portfolio, without the owner's go.

## Rulings (made while planning)

- **R1, one commit at the end.** The pre-commit hook runs every guard on the working tree, including "the committed
  page is a fresh build" and the publish staleness gates (`site/SCAN_PUBLISHED`, `site/PUBLISHED`). A commit of
  builder changes without a rebuilt AND republished page is refused, so tasks 1-5 run their guards and do NOT
  commit; task 6 publishes and commits once. Cost if wrong: none, the clone holds the work.
- **R2, publish does not wait for the fc-10 absorb.** The spec ordered "absorb lands first". Every absorb is
  already followed by the routine fc-08 re-import and scan republish (Stage566 K4b), which refreshes path A's
  figures. So this feature publishes with whatever import is current, and the next routine republish moves the
  figures. Cost if wrong: path A shows the pre-2026-10-30 figures until that routine runs.
- **R3, a step fc-08 cannot evidence shows "IN NEXUS".** `built: None`, `evidence: []`. A3 (queue re-review), B3
  (absorb the flag) and B4 (doctrine) happen in fc-10 or a toolkit, and the fc-10 export does not carry queue
  re-reviews or (until one exists) flags.
- **R4, the old "Next: NOT BUILT" list is removed.** Both of its items are built (K3 red flags, K2 queue
  re-reviews); they now appear as path B and step A3. The section becomes "Known limits, and why it can be trusted".

```python
          "question": "The only path that can end in new detection code. Six stages, each an owner command that "
                      "refuses to run until the one before is complete."}


def _figures(iv: dict) -> dict:
    """The live figure under each path step, from impact_view alone (spec §3). Never typed."""
    n_b = iv["flags"] + iv["flags_in_doctrine"]
    b12 = "Built, not yet used" if n_b == 0 else "%d flag(s) approved" % n_b
    return {
        "A1": "%d corroborations across %d typologies" % (iv["corroborations"], iv["typologies"]),
        "A2": "%d product re-reviews raised" % iv["rereviews"],
        "A3": "The rule only: the export does not carry queue re-reviews",
        "A4": "%d closed · %d open" % (iv["rereviews"] - iv["open"], iv["open"]),
        "A5": ("Absorbed through %s" % iv["absorbed_on"]) if iv["absorbed_on"] else "Not yet absorbed",
        "B1": b12, "B2": b12,
        "B3": "%d awaiting doctrine" % iv["flags"],
        "B4": "%d in doctrine" % iv["flags_in_doctrine"],
    }


def _paths(inp: dict) -> dict:
    fig = _figures(impact_view(inp["impact"]))
    return {k: {"steps": [dict({x: v for x, v in s.items() if x != "evidence"},
                               label="%s%d" % (k, s["n"]), figure=fig["%s%d" % (k, s["n"])]) for s in p["steps"]]}
            for k, p in inp["paths"].items()}
```

  `_paths` calls `_figures` through the module global, so the `path-figure` mutation's reassignment of

  `"paths": copy.deepcopy(PATHS),`. In `payload()`, beside `"pipeline": _pipeline(inp, links),` add
  `"paths": _paths(inp),`.

```python
def _head(p: dict) -> str:
    return '<h2>%s</h2>\n<p class="sub" style="font-size:13px;color:var(--muted)">%s</p>' % (
        html.escape(p["title"]), html.escape(p["question"]))


def build(inp: dict) -> str:
    data = json.dumps(payload(inp), ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).replace("</", "<\\/")
    heads = {k: _head(p) for k, p in inp["paths"].items()}
    return (TEMPLATE.replace("__PAYLOAD__", data).replace("__RUN__", html.escape(RUN_ID))
            .replace("__FIG_PATHS__", three_paths_svg()).replace("__FIG_STEPS__", steps_svg())
            .replace("__PATH_A__", heads.get("A", "")).replace("__PATH_B__", heads.get("B", ""))
            .replace("__PATH_C__", _head(PATH_C)))
```

```python
    ("Quotes must be on the page", "A claim whose quote cannot be found word for word on its source page blocks "
                                   "acceptance."),
    ("One-way crossings", "NEXUS reads fc-08's approvals; fc-08 imports NEXUS's library, proposals and impact. Each "
                          "import records the other side's commit and file hash."),
]
LIMITS = [
    ("Engine built is the owner's word", "The command records the commit it is given but does not inspect it. The "
                                         "real gate is live, which checks the product and the release record."),
    ("Absorb takes every approved link at once", "It cannot take a single advisory."),
    ("One re-review per link, not per case", "Three advisories linked to one typology give its case three separate "
                                             "re-reviews."),
    ("Actor names are labels", "The owner and supervisor names are written by the command, not checked against a "
                               "login."),
]


def _changes_html() -> str:
    head = "".join("<th>%s</th>" % html.escape(c) for c in CHANGES_COLS)
    body = "".join('<tr data-path="%s">%s</tr>' % (k, "".join("<td>%s</td>" % html.escape(c) for c in row))
                   for k, row in zip(CHANGES_KEYS, CHANGES))
    return ('<div style="overflow-x:auto"><table class="changes"><thead><tr>%s</tr></thead><tbody>%s</tbody>'
            '</table></div>' % (head, body))


def _list_html(items: list) -> str:
    return '<ul style="margin:8px 0 0;padding-left:18px;font-size:13px;color:var(--fg-2)">%s</ul>' % "".join(
        "<li><b>%s.</b> %s</li>" % (html.escape(t), html.escape(d)) for t, d in items)
```
